$description: Everline v0.1 candidate tokens derived from works/72ppi/everline_p1.svg. These values are drafts, not frozen decisions.

confirmedRules: Component sizes scale in 8 px steps while preserving internal proportions.

gray-800.$description: Observed subdued foreground and border candidate.

gray-500.$description: Batch 1 candidate (added 2026-08-04, GitHub issue #35, backfilled from an existing SVG value). works/everline-components-master.svg's own stylesheet defines .alert-body { fill: #b8b8b8 } for c-inline-alert's body/description text — lighter than gray-600 (#666666) so it stays legible as body copy on the #333333 alert card, but deliberately not as bright as off-white (#F2F2F2), which the same stylesheet reserves for .alert-title. No existing base color matched this value; same 'add the literal the SVG already draws, do not force it onto an existing role' precedent as gray-850's own addition.

gray-850.$description: Batch 2 candidate (added 2026-07-23, backfilled from an existing SVG value). Recessed container shade sitting between canvas (#1A1A1A) and gray-900/surface (#333333), used in the approved batch-2 SVG exclusively for Kanban column bodies so cards read as sitting on top of the column rather than blending into it. Never formalized into the token file when the SVG was drawn, which caused works/html/batch2/ to reuse background-surface for both the column and its cards, flattening the two into one indistinguishable color.

off-white.$description: Observed switch thumb and light foreground.

foreground-disabled.$description: Off-white foreground, combined with opacity.disabled (not baked into the color as 8-digit hex alpha) so the value stays portable to tools like Illustrator that don't reliably support #RRGGBBAA. Updated 2026-07-19 per user feedback: the prior value (gray-800 #444444, solid) had too little contrast against the gray-600 disabled surface, making disabled controls hard to read as buttons at all rather than clearly-but-legibly muted.

background-overlay.$description: Unified surface for floating/overlay panels (Select and Split-button menu, Menu/Context menu, Tooltip, Modal). Added 2026-07-19 to replace 4 previously uncoordinated values (background-subdued, background-surface, a direct gray-800 reference, and Modal's unaliased #222222) that gave visually-similar floating panels inconsistent depth and, worse, borrowed background-subdued's 'disabled' semantic for interactive menu surfaces. Chosen over gray-800 specifically because gray-800 is border-default — reusing it would make every overlay panel's border invisible against its own fill.

foreground-subdued.$description: Batch 2 candidate (2026-07-20). Medium-emphasis text role (table headers, sidebar section labels, task-card meta text). Backfills a semantic token for a role several existing components (e.g. component.tabs.foreground-default) reached directly into color.base.gray-700 for, bypassing the semantic layer contrary to the project's own token-naming convention. Purely additive — does not change any existing component's rendered value.

focus.$description: Batch 4 candidate (2026-07-30, added during PR review). The gap between a focus ring and the thing it marks was already an undocumented magic number repeated across batch 2 and batch 3 CSS; this gives it a name. Global rather than per-component because every focusable component needs the same gap, which is exactly the cross-component condition AGENTS.md requires before adding a shared value.

ring-offset.$description: One magnitude, two directions — the direction is a usage rule, not a second value. Standalone controls (buttons, range inputs, the popover close control) draw the ring OUTWARD at this offset. Elements that sit flush inside a row or grid (Accordion triggers, calendar day cells) draw it INWARD, i.e. this value negated, so the ring can't overlap its neighbours. Text-like fields use an inset box-shadow instead of an outline and therefore no offset at all. Distinct from border.width-focus (2px): that is the ring's thickness, this is its distance from the element, and they are free to diverge. Existing batch 2/3 CSS still hard-codes the same 2px; migrating it is a separate mechanical change.

motion.$description: Candidate (2026-07-19). No component's open/close or hover transition has been visually specified yet; these are placeholder values pending real product validation, added because Split button, Modal and Tooltip already reference 'needs animation' in spec text without any backing token.

duration-base.$description: Open/close transitions: dropdown, menu, tooltip, modal.

duration-slow.$description: Reserved for larger layout shifts; not yet used by any drawn component.

duration-loop.$description: Batch 3 candidate (2026-07-27), added for component.spinner's continuous rotation. Deliberately NOT reusing duration-slow (320ms): every existing duration-* token times a one-shot open/close transition, and 320ms for a full 360° spin reads as a fast, jittery flicker rather than a calm rotation. This is the first continuously-looping animation Everline has drawn, so it gets its own shared primitive (reusable by future loop animations, e.g. skeleton shimmer) instead of forcing an ill-fitting reuse of a differently-purposed value.

reduced-motion-rule.$value: prefers-reduced-motion: replace all open/close and hover transitions with an instant state change; never delay keyboard interaction on an animation.
reduced-motion-rule.$description: Generalizes the reduced-motion note already written for Split button to apply to every animated component (Modal, Tooltip, Menu, Select, Toast).

layer.$description: Candidate stacking order (2026-07-19) for components that render outside normal document flow. Added because Everline now has 5 distinct overlay-type components (Select/Split-button/Menu panels, Tooltip, Modal+backdrop, Toast) with no defined order for when they coexist (e.g. a toast confirming an action taken inside an open modal). Values are placeholder integers, not CSS z-index requirements; needs product confirmation before treating as fixed.

overlay.$description: Page-level popovers: Select/Combobox panel, Split-button menu, Menu/Context menu.

tooltip.$description: Above overlay panels, since a tooltip can appear on a trigger inside an open menu/select.

modal.$description: Just above its own backdrop. A tooltip rendered inside an open modal must still out-rank the modal locally; this global scale assumes tooltips are re-parented per context rather than fixed to a single number.

toast.$description: Topmost by convention, so transient feedback (e.g. 'deleted') stays visible even while a modal is open or closing. Product should confirm this is the intended behavior for Everline.

icon.$description: Candidate (2026-07-19). Formalizes the stroke-width already used consistently by every hand-drawn icon across the master sheet.

stroke-width.$description: Matches the .icon CSS class already used throughout works/everline-components-master.svg.

source.$value: shadcn/ui (via its bundled lucide-react integration) when the component is composed from shadcn/ui; otherwise the archived docs/lucide-icons-1.24.0 asset pack directly. Both resolve to the same Lucide icon family.
source.$description: User-specified constraint, 2026-07-19. Does not by itself confirm Taylor Kanban's tech stack; applies to whichever product ends up consuming Everline. Per AGENTS.md, third-party icon sets remain prototype/reference only — Everline still owns its own sizing, alignment and state rules layered on top (see size.icon-sm/icon-md and icon.stroke-width).

disabled.$description: Applied via fill-opacity/opacity (or CSS opacity), not baked into a color value. Used with color.semantic.foreground-disabled so disabled text stays legible-but-muted; kept as a separate multiplier rather than an alpha hex color for portability to tools (e.g. Illustrator) with inconsistent #RRGGBBAA support.

backdrop.$description: Batch 1 candidate (2026-07-19). Applied to color.base.canvas (or #000000) via fill-opacity for the modal scrim; not baked into the color value, for the same portability reason as opacity.disabled.

hover-overlay.$description: Batch 1 candidate (2026-07-19). Subtle white overlay for hover backgrounds on dark surfaces where a solid hover color isn't defined yet (e.g. Tabs hover), applied via fill="#ffffff" fill-opacity.

selected-overlay.$description: Batch 2 candidate (2026-07-20). Tinted selected-row background for component.list-item.* (List/Data table/Kanban column), applied to color.semantic.action-primary via fill-opacity. Deliberately a tint, not Select's existing solid action-primary fill — multi-row persistent selection (a table, a list) reads as a stack of buttons if every selected row is solid-filled; this only applies to the 3 new components, Select/Split-button/Menu are unchanged in this pass.

dragging.$description: Batch 2 cross-component decision (2026-07-23). Applied to the element currently being dragged (Card, Task card). Deliberately lighter than opacity.disabled (0.55) — a dragged item is still the active focus of the interaction, it should read as 'lifted', not muted/unavailable like a disabled control. Paired with a border.width-focus / border-focus outline instead of a drop shadow, per Everline's low-decoration principle: shadows read poorly against this dark palette, an outline doesn't.

control-md.$description: Observed standard button and switch height.

tag-md.$description: Candidate compact component height snapped to the confirmed 8 px scale grid.

step.$description: Confirmed component enlargement and reduction step.

button.$description: Observed from the primary button family in works/72ppi/everline_p1.svg.

width-reference.$description: Observed reference width; production width may grow with content.

foreground.$description: White. Only the primary and danger variants use this — verified against works/everline-components-master.svg c-button, where those two are the only variants with an explicit fill="#fff" text override.

foreground-neutral.$description: Batch 1 (issue #17) gap found during P0 token audit, 2026-07-30. The neutral and outline variants' label text in c-button has no fill override, so it inherits the sheet's default .label fill (#f2f2f2, off-white / foreground-primary) — a different value from `foreground` (white / foreground-inverse) above, which only the primary/danger variants actually use. The token file previously declared a single `foreground` for the whole component, which would have painted neutral/outline text white instead of the SVG's actual off-white.

foreground.$description: Batch 1 (issues #30) gap found during P0 token audit, 2026-07-31. White. Only the primary and danger variants use this — verified against works/everline-components-master.svg c-icon-button, where those two are the only variants with an explicit fill="#fff" text override, same split already found and fixed on component.button.

foreground-neutral.$description: Batch 1 (issue #30) gap, same pattern as component.button.foreground-neutral: the neutral and outline variants' placeholder text in c-icon-button has no fill override, so it inherits the sheet's default .label fill (#f2f2f2, off-white / foreground-primary), not white.

foreground-disabled.$description: Batch 1 (issue #30) gap. Verified against c-icon-button's disabled variant: fill="#f2f2f2" fill-opacity="0.55", the same off-white + opacity.disabled formula as component.button.foreground-disabled.

border-width.$description: Batch 1 (issue #30) gap. 2px, matching the outline variant's stroke-width="2" in c-icon-button (rect x=1 y=1 width=46 height=46 stroke="#598ae8" stroke-width="2").

border-focus.$description: Batch 1 (issue #30) gap. Matches the outline variant's stroke="#598ae8" in the same SVG group.

thumb-inset.$description: Observed optical inset; not a component scale step.

border.$description: Batch 1 (issue #17) gap found during P0 token audit, 2026-07-30. works/everline-components-master.svg c-checkbox draws the unchecked state with stroke="#444" (gray-800 / border-default) — an existing semantic token that was never aliased under component.checkbox. Checked/indeterminate/disabled states have no stroke, so this only applies to unchecked.

border-width.$description: 1px, matching the unchecked state's stroke-width="1" in the same SVG group.

border.$description: Batch 1 (issue #32) gap found during P0 token audit, 2026-07-31, same pattern as component.checkbox.border: works/everline-components-master.svg c-radio draws the unchecked state with stroke="#444" (gray-800 / border-default), never aliased under component.radio. Checked/disabled states have no stroke, so this only applies to unchecked.

border-width.$description: 1px, matching the unchecked state's stroke-width="1" in the same SVG group.

width-reference.$description: Observed source width; scaling changes this baseline in 8 px steps.

foreground.$description: Batch 1 (issue #33) gap found during P0 token audit, 2026-07-31. White. Matches c-split-button's main label and chevron icon, both fill="#fff".

menu-foreground.$description: Batch 1 (issue #33) gap. Off-white. The two drawn menu item labels in c-split-button's open group have no fill override, so they inherit the sheet's default .label fill — the same generic default-text role Popover already declared its own explicit alias for (component.popover.foreground), added here for the same CSS-authoring clarity rather than leaving it an unstated inherited value.

divider-color.$description: Batch 1 (issue #33) gap. Backfilled from the approved SVG's own divider line (stroke="#4a76c9" between the main action and disclosure regions in both closed and open c-split-button groups) — a distinct value from action-primary (#598ae8), needed because a plain border-default (#444) or action-primary line would not read against the same action-primary fill it sits on. Same backfill-an-already-drawn-value treatment as color.base.gray-850 for Kanban column; not a new design decision, just previously untokenized.

layer.$description: Batch 1 (issue #33) gap. Same candidate-recorded-not-validated caveat already noted on component.popover.layer: layer.overlay's coexistence order with Tooltip/Modal/Toast remains unverified, and this pilot does not render more than one overlay type at once either.

foreground-disabled.$description: Batch 1 (issue #17) gap found during P0 token audit, 2026-07-30. Text input's own SVG group never drew a disabled state (design-system-v0.1-draft.md lists it under 'regex needed but not drawn'), so this cannot be verified against c-text-input directly. Reused instead from component.number-input.field-foreground-disabled, which already extends Text input's own field and had this exact disabled treatment (background stays the solid token colour, only foreground combines with opacity.disabled via color-mix) human-reviewed and pixel-validated in batch 3 (see docs/design-system-v0.1-batch3-draft.md). Not a new visual decision.

scrollbar-width.$description: Observed optical width; verify before implementation.

foreground.$description: Batch 1 (issue #17) gap found during P0 token audit, 2026-07-30. component.textarea had no typed-text foreground token at all. NOT verified against c-textarea directly — corrected 2026-07-30 during PR #29 review: both drawn c-textarea examples only render placeholder-style text (fill="#4d4d4d", the same value as placeholder below), never a filled/typed example, so there is no SVG-drawn value for typed text to check against. This is a G1-accepted extension decision, not an SVG measurement: same value as component.text-input.foreground since both fields share the same generic default-text role, reused rather than invented.

placeholder.$description: Batch 1 gap. Verified directly against c-textarea's placeholder text fill="#4d4d4d" (gray-700) in the master SVG — same value component.text-input.placeholder already uses, but textarea never had its own alias.

foreground-disabled.$description: Batch 1 gap, same reuse rationale as component.text-input.foreground-disabled above: no disabled state was drawn for Textarea either, so this reuses the already-reviewed Number-input-field disabled treatment rather than inventing one.

border-width-focus.$description: Batch 1 gap. Textarea's own SVG group (resizable/scrollable) does not draw a focused example, but the design draft's text explicitly calls for the same 2px blue focus border as Text input, and every sibling text-entry component in this system (Text input, Search field, Number input's field) already uses this exact technique. Reused, not a new decision.

border-focus.$description: Batch 1 gap, same reuse rationale as border-width-focus above.

search-field.$description: Batch 3 candidate (2026-07-27, GitHub issue #6, component 2/8). Extends component.text-input's structure (height/radius/background/foreground/placeholder/border-focus all identical values) with a leading search icon and a content-conditional trailing clear button. Every value below was verified against the reviewed candidate in works/everline-components-batch3.svg (c-search-field group) before being added, per AGENTS.md's token-before-use rule. No width token, same reasoning already applied to component.text-input (width set by container).

icon-color.$description: Same tone as placeholder — the search icon is decorative/muted, not a state indicator, so it doesn't get its own color identity.

icon-inset.$description: Distance from the field's edge to the search icon, and from the field's edge to the clear button.

padding-inline-start.$description: Reserves room for the leading search icon: icon-inset (16px) + icon-size (16px) + content-gap (8px) = 40px. Always applied (the search icon is never hidden).

padding-inline-end.$description: Trailing padding when the field is empty (no clear button) — same value component.text-input.padding-inline already uses.

padding-inline-end-filled.$description: Trailing padding once a clear button is present (filled/focused-with-content), mirroring padding-inline-start's derivation (icon-inset + icon-size + content-gap).

select.$description: Batch 1 candidate (2026-07-19). Reuses text-input-like trigger and split-button-like menu surface.

search-match-highlight.$description: Combobox variant: color applied to the matched substring in filtered results.

hover-background.$description: Combine with opacity.hover-overlay via fill-opacity, same technique as tabs.hover-background. Changed 2026-07-19 from a solid gray-700 fill because gray-700 is now background-overlay itself (menu's own panel fill) — a solid hover row in the same color would be invisible.

max-width.$description: Candidate wrap width; not yet product-validated.

modal.$description: Batch 1 candidate (2026-07-19). Focus trapping is a behavioral requirement (see spec), not something a static vector token can express.

background.$description: Changed 2026-07-19 from an unaliased #222222 (the only token in this file that skipped the base -> semantic -> component pattern) to the shared background-overlay token.

backdrop-color.$description: Combine with opacity.backdrop via fill-opacity, not a baked alpha hex.

toast.$description: Batch 1 candidate (2026-07-19). Auto-dismiss timing not yet defined.

height.$description: 56 px, one 8 px step above the standard control-md height.

danger-icon-size.$description: Solid-fill circular danger icon, distinct from the bare-stroke icons used by the other toast variants.

list-item.$description: Batch 2 candidate (2026-07-20). Shared row language for List, Data table, and Kanban column's task-card rows only — deliberately NOT retrofitted onto Select/Split-button/Menu's existing selected-item visuals in this pass (see docs/design-system-v0.1-batch2-draft.md for the retrofit-later note).

row-gap.$description: Optical gap between adjoining individually-rounded rows, per 處處是圓; not a component scale step, same treatment as component.switch.thumb-inset.

background-hover.$description: Combine with opacity.hover-overlay via fill-opacity, same technique as tabs/menu hover.

background-selected.$description: Combine with opacity.selected-overlay via fill-opacity — a tint, not a solid fill.

indicator-width.$description: Left accent bar on selected rows; a decorative accent, distinct from border.width-*.

sidebar.$description: Batch 2 candidate (2026-07-20). Single component with expanded and collapsed (rail) modes.

width-collapsed.$description: Candidate rail width; unverified. Also the minimum width when resizing — dragging narrower than the collapsed rail doesn't make sense, at that point it should just collapse.

width-max.$description: Batch 2 cross-component decision (2026-07-23). Resize ceiling; not visually validated, picked as a reasonable cap so the sidebar can't crowd out the main content area. No snapping/presets in this pass.

notification-dot-color.$description: Candidate; whether notification dots should carry primary or danger semantics is flagged open, not decided in this pass.

card.$description: Batch 2 candidate (2026-07-20). Generic content card, distinct from component.task-card.

border-error.$description: Reuses Inline alert's 4px indicator-bar language rather than inventing a new error treatment.

data-table.$description: Batch 2 candidate (2026-07-20). Single row-height only in this pass; density and pagination are intentionally not yet defined.

kanban-column.$description: Batch 2 candidate (2026-07-20). Must render as individually-rounded cards with gaps — never the flat/table layout referenced in works/TaylorConceptMockup1.svg, which is a structural reference only, not a style source.

width.$description: Corrected 2026-07-23 to match the value actually drawn and user-approved in the 2026-07-20 SVG review (pixel-measured from exports/everline-components-batch2.png); the prior 320px was an unverified candidate that was never what got reviewed. 288 still satisfies the 8px scale grid (288 = 36 x 8).

background.$description: Added 2026-07-23. Column body fill, deliberately darker than component.card/task-card's background-surface so Task cards visually separate from the column instead of blending into it — backfilled from the approved SVG, which used this shade but never had it captured as a token (see color.base.gray-850).

task-card.$description: Batch 2 candidate (2026-07-20). Extends component.card.*; status-dot colors constrained to the existing approved palette, no unapproved success/warning hues.

status-dot-done.$description: No approved success/green token yet; reuses action-primary blue to mean 'complete' pending a real success-color decision.

assignee-avatar-size.$description: Lightweight ad-hoc avatar placeholder for the assignee candidate field — deliberately not component.avatar.*; Avatar/Avatar group remains a second-phase candidate, out of v0.1 scope (tracked in GitHub Issues, not this file).

spinner.$description: Batch 3 candidate (2026-07-27, GitHub issue #5). Indeterminate-only circular loading indicator, three sizes. Backfilled from the reviewed works/everline-components-batch3.svg candidate — sizes deliberately reuse existing scale/size tokens instead of inventing new numbers, since the drawn diameters already matched them exactly.

size-sm.$description: 24px. Inline usage next to text (e.g. a loading row label).

stroke-width-lg.$description: Distinct from icon.stroke-width (2px, for flat line icons) — a spinner ring needs a heavier stroke to stay legible while rotating, roughly scaling with its diameter.

track-color.$description: Same direct base-color reference pattern already used by component.text-input.placeholder.

overlay-backdrop-color.$description: Full-page variant only; reuses Modal's exact backdrop treatment (combine with opacity.backdrop) rather than inventing a second dimming value.

progress.$description: Batch 3 candidate (2026-07-27, GitHub issue #5). Horizontal progress bar: determinate, indeterminate and error variants. Backfilled from works/everline-components-batch3.svg. No fixed width token — a progress bar's width is set by its container (modal, toolbar, etc.), same reasoning already applied to component.text-input having no width token.

breadcrumb.$description: Batch 3 candidate (2026-07-28, GitHub issue #7, component 3/8). Backfilled from the human-reviewed works/everline-components-batch3.svg c-breadcrumb group after a 2026-07-28 review round that replaced an initial flush-left layout with per-item centered hit-area slots (each item's text centered within its own slot instead of hugging the chevron) — slot widths were verified against Chrome's own getBBox() text measurement, not eyeballed, so the visual gap from any item's text edge to its nearest chevron is a uniform 21px. No new colors: every foreground value reuses an existing semantic token.

foreground-current.$description: Same value as foreground-hover; current is distinguished from default by font-weight (see font.weight-semibold), not a unique color — current never hovers so there's no ambiguity.

separator-size.$description: 16px conceptual icon box; the drawn chevron glyph itself is narrower (6px wide), same convention as other Everline icons where the box is larger than the glyph ink.

item-padding-inline.$description: 8px each side, inside an item's own hit-area slot — the slot width is therefore the item's rendered text width + 16px, not a fixed value.

item-gap.$description: 32px fixed gap between adjoining item slots; the separator is centered inside this gap.

hover-background.$description: Combine with opacity.hover-overlay via fill-opacity, same technique as Tabs/Menu/List-item hover.

ellipsis-size.$description: Collapsed-state truncation trigger hit area, 32px. Cross-checked 2026-07-29 against this system's other small interactive elements — matches scale.component-heights.xs exactly, the same size already used by component.checkbox.size and component.radio.size (both 32px); deliberately not size.tag-md's 40px, which is a compact component-height value, not a small hit-area value. No longer a standalone candidate literal.

ellipsis-dot-size.$description: Diameter of each of the 3 dots representing the collapsed items.

number-input.$description: Batch 3 candidate (2026-07-28, GitHub issue #8, component 4/8). Backfilled from the human-reviewed works/everline-components-batch3.svg c-number-input group. Extends component.text-input (field) and component.icon-button (decrement/increment) by direct alias rather than redeclaring their values, per the issue's own scope note. Only the field width and the button-to-field gap are new candidate values; every color reuses an existing semantic token.

field-width.$description: Sized for 2-3 digit values only, not on the 8px scale grid (an intentional exception, same as component.number-input's sibling text-field-width candidates elsewhere in this file). Verified 2026-07-29 with a canvas measureText probe against the graduated field's actual computed font: a 3-digit value ('999') measures 26.6px wide at the base 16px font size and only 40px even at 24px (1.5x base, this system's h2 size) — well inside the 80px field with no scrollWidth overflow at either size, so no truncation risk at any realistic font-size within this system's scale.

gap.$description: 8px gap between decrement button / field / increment button — each keeps its own rounding rather than fusing into one shape, per 處處是圓.

field-foreground-disabled.$description: Combine with opacity.disabled, same technique as Search field's disabled text.

button-background-disabled.$description: Applies per-button (min/max reached disables only the corresponding button) as well as to the whole component when fully disabled.

button-icon-color.$description: First time Icon button's own icon color has been decided (the master sheet only ever showed icon-button with a text-label placeholder, never a real icon) — scoped under component.number-input rather than added to the shared component.icon-button group, matching how Search field scoped its own icon-color instead of editing component.text-input.

button-icon-color-disabled.$description: Combine with opacity.disabled, same technique as Search field's disabled icon.

slider.$description: Batch 4 candidate (2026-07-30, GitHub issue #9). Backfilled from the human-approved works/everline-components-batch4.svg c-slider group after its G1 review. Extends component.progress's track geometry (identical 8px height, pill radius and gray-700 track) and component.switch's thumb language, but stays a separate component. No new color was introduced.

track-height.$description: 8px. Deliberately aliased to Progress's height rather than re-declaring space.1 - the two share a track shape and should move together if it ever changes.

track-color.$description: gray-700, the same unfilled-track role Progress bar already defined.

fill-disabled.$description: The approved SVG turns the filled portion to background-subdued (#666666) rather than tinting it, matching component.button.background-disabled. The track itself stays gray-700 so the control keeps its shape.

thumb-size.$description: 24px, measured from the approved SVG (r=12 circle).

thumb.$description: off-white, the same thumb role as Switch.

thumb-disabled.$description: Combine with opacity.disabled. NOTE this differs from component.switch.thumb-disabled (a solid gray-600): the approved Slider candidate keeps the off-white thumb and mutes it, the same technique Search field and Number input use for disabled content. Flagged as a cross-component inconsistency for review - Switch was deliberately not retrofitted in this pass.

focus-ring-width.$description: Solid ring hugging the thumb with no gap: thumb 24px -> outer diameter 32px. Human decision 2026-07-30 during G1, replacing an earlier 2px stroke + 2px offset which at 24px read as a detached hairline. Deliberately NOT aliased to component.switch.thumb-inset or component.list-item.row-gap even though both are also 4px - those are optical insets/gaps, an unrelated meaning. Also not border.width-focus (2px), because this is a filled ring, not a stroke.

step-marker-size.$description: Corrected 2026-07-30 after PR review: this previously aliased component.breadcrumb.ellipsis-dot-size, but the two are only coincidentally both 4px. A breadcrumb dot represents collapsed navigation items and a slider marker represents a discrete step; nothing would make them need to change together, and aliasing on a shared number would couple them for future edits. Same reasoning already applied to focus-ring-width below.

step-marker-gap.$description: 8px from the track edge to the marker row.

value-label-width.$description: 40px. Candidate variant only - a value label is not required for v0.1.

value-label-height.$description: Candidate variant only. Numerically equal to size.icon-md but declared rather than aliased, because this is a box height, not an icon box.

value-label-gap.$description: 8px between the label's bottom edge and the thumb's top edge. Corrected during the 2026-07-30 review - the first draft overlapped the thumb by 4px.

track-length-reference.$description: Catalog reference length only; production width is set by the container, the same reasoning that left component.progress and component.text-input without a width token.

accordion.$description: Batch 4 candidate (2026-07-30, GitHub issue #10). Backfilled from the human-approved works/everline-components-batch4.svg c-accordion group. Single-open vs multi-open is an interaction setting, NOT a token: both modes are visually identical and deliberately share every value below. No new color was introduced.

trigger-height.$description: 48px minimum; grows if a title wraps.

item-radius.$description: 8px, the same individually-rounded-row language as List and Data table rows.

item-gap.$description: 4px between adjoining items. Chosen over a divider line: Everline separates adjoining rounded rows with a gap, so no divider-width token is created - the plan required picking one of the two, not both.

content-padding.$description: 16px above and below the expanded panel's content, inside the same rounded box as its trigger.

background-hover.$description: Combine with opacity.hover-overlay, the same technique as Tabs, Menu, List-item and Breadcrumb hover. Aliased to color.base.white rather than repeating the literal #ffffff those five older tokens still carry — the base layer already owns this value. Sweeping the existing five onto the same alias is a separate, purely mechanical change and was deliberately left out of this batch.

foreground-disabled.$description: Combine with opacity.disabled. The disabled trigger keeps background-surface instead of switching to background-subdued the way disabled buttons do - a row is not a filled button, and lightening it would make the disabled item the most prominent thing in the list.

popover.$description: Batch 4 candidate (2026-07-30, GitHub issue #11). Backfilled from the human-approved works/everline-components-batch4.svg c-popover group. Non-modal floating panel opened by an explicit click on a trigger. Hard requirement carried from the plan: it reuses the shared color.semantic.background-overlay surface instead of inventing a parallel floating-panel color. No shadow token was added - the approved candidate expresses depth with the overlay fill against canvas, consistent with the low-decoration reasoning already recorded on opacity.dragging.

radius.$description: 16px, the same as component.select.menu-radius and component.modal.radius.

anchor-gap.$description: 8px from the trigger's edge to the arrow's tip.

arrow-color.$description: Always identical to the panel fill. The approved candidate draws no panel border, so the arrow has no border edge to match either.

close-control-size.$description: 32px hit area. Aliased to the 8px-grid xs height rather than component.icon-button.size (48px), which would dominate a 16px-padded panel - the same 32px hit-area decision Breadcrumb's ellipsis trigger already made.

action-height.$description: 40px in-panel action button, aliased to Modal's existing in-panel action height rather than the 48px standalone control height.

layer.$description: layer.overlay is still a candidate value and its coexistence order with Tooltip, Modal and Toast remains UNVERIFIED: the batch 4 prototype only renders one overlay type at a time, so it could not be verified there either. Recorded, not validated.

date-time-picker.$description: Batch 4 candidate (2026-07-30, GitHub issue #12). Backfilled from the human-approved works/everline-components-batch4.svg c-date-time-picker group. A composition, not a new primitive: the trigger is component.text-input plus component.icon-button and the panel is component.popover, all reused by alias. Only the calendar-specific geometry below is new. v0.1 excludes lunar calendars, multi-locale and multi-calendar formatting, time zones, week numbers, preset ranges and recurrence.

panel-width.$description: Derived, not chosen: 7 x calendar-cell-size (40) + 2 x component.popover.padding (16) = 312. Re-derive rather than hand-edit if either input changes.

calendar-cell-size.$description: 40px, on the 8px grid. Cells sit edge to edge with no gap so the grid keeps a predictable 40px pitch.

range-day-size.$description: Each in-between day gets its own 36px tinted circle, leaving a 4px gap at the 40px cell pitch (that gap equals component.list-item.row-gap). Human decision 2026-07-30 at G1, replacing a continuous 40px band whose square corners fought the circular endpoints and whose adjacent rows merged into one rectangle. Stated reason for choosing per-day circles: still easy to read as a range, and consistent with the round-everywhere design language.

range-background.$description: action-primary combined with opacity.selected-overlay (0.18) - a tint, aliased to the existing selected-row treatment rather than declaring a second one.

today-indicator-width.$description: 2px ring with no fill, so today never competes with selected.

outside-month-foreground.$description: Combine with opacity.disabled (0.55). Deliberately MORE legible than unavailable-foreground: an outside-month day is still clickable (it jumps months), an unavailable day is not.

unavailable-foreground.$description: gray-600 - the existing precedent for disabled text on an overlay panel. color.semantic.foreground-subdued cannot be used here: it resolves to gray-700, the same value as background-overlay, so it would be invisible on this panel.

weekday-foreground.$description: The same overlay-panel muted tone as unavailable-foreground, for the same invisibility reason.

month-nav-size.$description: 40px hit area for the previous/next month controls.

time-field-width.$description: Corrected 2026-07-30 during graduation, from the 128px the approved SVG implied. The SVG drew a static string (14:30) that fits 128px, but a real <input type="time"> renders in the user's locale: under zh-TW it shows a 上午/下午 prefix and asks for 104px of intrinsic width, which 128px clipped. Measured in Chrome: 104 (control) + 16 (clock icon) + 8 (space.1 gap) + 2 x 16 (space.2 padding) = 160, which is still on the 8px grid (20 x 8). The element's VALUE is always 24-hour HH:MM per the HTML spec — only the rendering is localized — so the documented value format is unchanged. This deviation from the approved candidate's geometry was accepted by the human at the 2026-07-30 G6 acceptance; the SVG was deliberately not redrawn, since a graduated sheet records what was approved rather than tracking later corrections.

trigger-field-width.$description: Catalog reference only - production width is set by the container, the same reasoning as component.text-input.

action-height.$description: 48px. Unlike component.popover.action-height (40px), the picker's confirm/cancel row sits at the bottom of a tall panel and uses the standard control height, as drawn and approved.

tag.$description: Batch 1 candidate (2026-08-03, GitHub issue #34, component 8/15 of issue #17's list). Backfilled from works/everline-components-master.svg's c-badge-tag group (tag-neutral/tag-accent/tag-danger/tag-outline/tag-disabled/tag-removable instances) — this component had zero prior token coverage, so every value below is a first-time addition, not a gap fix. The outline variant is the spec's selectable filter tag (docs/design-system-v0.1-draft.md: 'outline：低強度可選標籤'), wired as a real toggle button per the interaction requirement, but the SVG only ever drew one outline appearance — never a distinct selected/pressed look — so toggling does not change its visual (same 'undrawn state, not invented' treatment already applied to component.button's pressed/loading). No new colors: every fill reuses an existing semantic token, following the exact primary/danger-get-white vs neutral/outline-get-off-white split already established by component.button and component.icon-button; the leading dot and both icons use currentColor in CSS rather than a dedicated color token, since the SVG's own dot/icon fills always exactly matched their sibling label text's fill.

radius.$description: Half of size.tag-md (40px), per the design draft's confirmed rule that pill radius derives from half the component height (處處是圓). Matches every tag-* rect's own rx="20" in the SVG exactly. Declared as a literal rather than aliased to radius.pill (999px), the same reasoning component.button/icon-button/text-input/split-button already applied by declaring radius.control (24px, half of 48px) instead of reusing radius.pill.

gap.$description: 8px gap between the leading dot/icon and the label text, and between the label text and a trailing remove control.

icon-size.$description: 16px. Shared by the danger variant's leading icon and the removable variant's remove icon. Matches docs/design-system-v0.1-draft.md's icon-system rule '緊湊情境（如 badge 前導圖示...）16 px' — this is that rule's first consumer.

dot-size.$description: Diameter of the accent variant's leading selection dot (SVG circle r="4"). Declared as a literal, not aliased to space.1, for the same reason component.task-card.status-dot-size and component.sidebar.notification-dot-size are literals — a dot's diameter and a spacing value are different concepts that only coincidentally share a number.

foreground.$description: White. Verified against c-badge-tag: tag-accent and tag-danger are the only two variants with an explicit fill="#fff" on their label text (and, on tag-accent, its dot; on tag-danger, its icon stroke) — the same primary/danger-variant-gets-white split already found on component.button and component.icon-button.

foreground-neutral.$description: Off-white. tag-neutral, tag-outline and tag-removable's label text (and tag-removable's own remove icon, stroke="#f2f2f2") have no fill override, so they inherit the sheet's default .label fill — the same neutral/outline-gets-off-white split already found on component.button and component.icon-button.

foreground-disabled.$description: Off-white, combined with opacity.disabled via the same color-mix technique as every other disabled component in this file. Matches tag-disabled's own fill="#f2f2f2" fill-opacity="0.55" exactly.

border-width.$description: 2px, matching the outline variant's stroke-width="2" in c-badge-tag (rect x=1 y=1 width=110 height=38 stroke="#598ae8").

border-focus.$description: Matches the outline variant's stroke="#598ae8" in the same SVG group.

hit-area-size.$description: 48px. Backfills docs/design-system-v0.1-draft.md's own accessibility requirement for Badge/Tag ('可互動 tag 的實際命中區使用 48 × 48 px；40 px 視覺高度由上下各 4 px 的透明 hit area 補足'). Applies only to the outline variant, the one interactive whole-tag control here (a selectable filter chip) — not drawn in the SVG. This is an extension decision PENDING G1 review (Badge/Tag has not passed G1 as of this writing), reusing the existing standard control size rather than inventing a new number, the same size and reasoning component.popover.close-control-size and Breadcrumb's ellipsis trigger already used for their own nested hit areas — reusing an already-G1-approved value's reasoning does not itself make this specific application G1-approved yet.

remove-control-size.$description: Hit area for the removable variant's nested remove button. Not drawn in the SVG (which only shows the icon's own ~20px glyph, no separate hit-area indication) — an extension decision PENDING G1 review (Badge/Tag has not passed G1 as of this writing), same value and reasoning as component.popover.close-control-size: a nested dismiss control inside a smaller component, where the full component.icon-button.size (48px) would be wider than the 40px tag it sits inside.

remove-icon-offset.$description: PR #46 review (opus) found a real, CDP-measured regression: giving the remove control its own 32px hit area on top of the tag's full padding-inline (16px) put the icon's rendered centre 32px from the pill's right edge, 9px further in than the SVG's own tag-removable group, where the X icon (path 'M116 15l10 10 M126 15l-10 10', bounding box centre x=(116+126)/2=121) sits 144-121=23px from the rect's right edge (width=144). Human decision 2026-08-03: keep the 32px hit area (accessibility requirement, not negotiable) but restore icon position fidelity to the approved SVG by shrinking just the removable variant's own trailing padding-inline-end to (remove-icon-offset − half of remove-control-size) = 23 − 16 = 7px via CSS calc() against these two tokens directly — its leading side and every other variant keep the normal component.tag.padding-inline (16px) unchanged.

inline-alert.$description: Batch 1 candidate (2026-08-04, GitHub issue #35, component 9/15 of issue #17's list). Backfilled from works/everline-components-master.svg's c-inline-alert group (alert-info/alert-danger/alert-neutral instances, lines 294-325) — this component had zero prior token coverage, so every value below is a first-time addition, not a gap fix. Only info/danger/neutral are drawn; docs/design-system-v0.1-draft.md's own Inline alert section already states no success/warning color exists yet and none is added here. The draft's prose said the status icon is 24px, but the SVG draws a stroked circle r="14" (28px diameter, measured the same 2 x r method already used for component.tag.dot-size) — the measured SVG value overrides the unverified draft number per AGENTS.md's graduation rule; docs/design-system-v0.1-draft.md is corrected to match in the same round. The neutral variant's rail (fill="#666", background-subdued) and its icon stroke ("#f2f2f2", foreground-primary) are NOT the same color, unlike info/danger where rail and icon share one token — this asymmetry is real in the SVG, not an oversight, and is captured as two separate tokens below. The SVG's own stylesheet also defines two different text colors, not one: .alert-title { fill: #f2f2f2 } (off-white, existing foreground-primary) and .alert-body { fill: #b8b8b8 } — the latter matches no existing base color, so color.base.gray-500 (#B8B8B8) is added alongside this component, the same 'add the literal, do not force it onto an existing role' precedent already used for color.base.gray-850. Font sizes: .alert-title's 17px does not match any existing font.size-* step (14/16/24), so it is declared as a new literal (title-size); .alert-body's 14px matches font.size-label exactly and is aliased instead of duplicated (body-size). PR #47 review (codex) found and this round fixed two real bugs: (1) the status icon rendered at 24.5px instead of 28px — see icon-render-margin's own $description; (2) the dismiss button's X glyph rendered 24px further from the card's right edge than the SVG (48px measured vs. the source's 24px) because the container's general padding-inline-end was applied on top of the button's own centring instead of being removed for that variant — fixed in styles.css, no token change needed for that specific fix. Also removed border-width/border-focus, which PR #47 review found were declared but never consumed by any CSS rule — the dismiss button's focus ring is fully satisfied by the file's existing global :focus-visible rule, so a component-specific alias with no consumer was dead weight, not a real gap.

min-height.$description: Card rect height in all three variants (rx="16" on a 760x96 rect). Declared as a minimum rather than a fixed height so real, potentially-wrapping title/body text does not force overflow or clipping — a structural robustness allowance, not a new visual, the same class of decision already applied to component.number-input's field width and component.search-field's layout during their own graduations.

radius.$description: 16px, matches every alert-* rect's own rx="16" exactly; radius.lg already exists and is reused as-is (same alias component.modal.radius and component.select.menu-radius use).

rail-width.$description: Rail rect width in all three variants.

rail-inset.$description: Left edge of the rail rect (x="12") in all three variants.

rail-radius.$description: Rail rect rx="2" — half of rail-width, the same 'radius derives from half of the element's own scaling dimension' reasoning already used for component.tag.radius (half of height), just applied to the rail's width instead of a component height.

content-start.$description: Distance from the card's left edge to the title/body text's own x position (both text x="80"), covering the rail (12px inset + 4px width) and the centred 28px status icon (centre cx="48") in a single measured value — implemented as the text column's own flex start position, not decomposed into sub-gaps the SVG does not directly evidence.

icon-size.$description: The status icon circle (info/neutral variants) is drawn as circle r="14" stroke-width="2" — diameter measured as 2 x r = 28px, the same 'diameter = 2 x radius' method already used for component.tag.dot-size (r="4" -> 8px). The danger variant's triangle icon (no circle) shares the same cx="48" cy="48" centre and a comparable bounding box, and is sized to the same token so all three variants' icons occupy one consistent slot. This corrects the design draft's previous, unmeasured '24 px' figure — see this token group's own $description.

icon-render-margin.$description: PR #47 review found the drawn circle rendering at 24.5px instead of the intended 28px: the icon SVG's viewBox (0 0 32 32, sized to also fit the wider danger triangle) was scaled down to fit a 28px CSS box, shrinking every unit including the 28-unit circle. Fix: the icon SVG's own rendered box is icon-size plus 2 x this margin (32px total, matching the 32-unit viewBox 1:1 so viewBox units and rendered pixels are equal), and this margin is subtracted from the icon's absolute horizontal offset so its visual centre stays put. Not an SVG-measured value — purely a rendering-implementation constant so the viewBox-to-pixel ratio stays 1:1.

title-body-gap.$description: 8px. Matches docs/design-system-v0.1-draft.md's own text ('標題與說明間距 8 px').

title-size.$description: The SVG stylesheet defines .alert-title { font-size: 17px }, which matches none of the existing font.size-label (14px) / size-body (16px) / size-title (24px) scale steps. Declared as a new literal here rather than rounding to an existing step, since 17px is what the approved SVG actually draws.

body-size.$description: 14px. .alert-body { font-size: 14px } matches the existing font.size-label token exactly, so this aliases it rather than adding a second literal.

foreground-title.$description: Off-white. Matches the SVG stylesheet's .alert-title { fill: #f2f2f2 }, shared by all three variants (no per-variant override).

foreground-body.$description: Matches the SVG stylesheet's .alert-body { fill: #b8b8b8 } exactly — deliberately NOT the same token as foreground-title. This is a real, first-documented use of a color the SVG already drew but no token previously covered (see color.base.gray-500's own $description); it is not a typo or an inconsistency to be unified with foreground-title.

rail-color-neutral.$description: Gray, not off-white. See this token group's own $description for why this differs from icon-color-neutral.

icon-color-neutral.$description: Off-white, not gray. alert-neutral's icon stroke is "#f2f2f2" while its own rail is "#666" — deliberately kept as two separate tokens rather than unified, since unifying either direction would contradict a value actually drawn in the SVG.

dismiss-control-size.$description: Not drawn as a separate hit-area shape in master.svg — only a bare X path remains at translate(712 24) with local coordinates 18,18 to 30,30. The older source works/everline-agent-components-v0.1.svg had an explicit 48x48 transparent hit-area rect at the same position (712-760 x 24-72, flush with the card's right edge), which master.svg dropped when it was redrawn. This token restores that 48px hit area, matching the existing size.control-md convention already used for nested dismiss controls elsewhere (component.popover.close-control-size). Extension decision PENDING G1 review (Inline alert has not passed G1 as of this writing) — only the info variant demonstrates a dismiss button in this round, since danger/neutral never drew one; not added to those two per 'undrawn visual, not invented.'

family-sans.$description: Confirmed UI font stack (user-confirmed 2026-07-19). The source SVG had converted text to outlines, so this could not be verified from the file alone; no longer a candidate value.
